title: Homily III — All creation escorts her to the tomb

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily III on the Dormition, cols. 757-760 (PDF leaves 420-421)

source_text:
Σήμερον ἀρχὴν λαμβάνει δευτέρας ὑπάρξεως ὑπὸ τοῦ δόντος αὐτῇ τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆς προτέρας ὑπάρξεως, ἡ δοῦσα δευτέρας ἀρχήν, τῆς σωματικῆς λέγω ὑπάρξεως, τῷ μὴ ἐσχηκότι ἀρχὴν χρονικὴν τῆς προτέρας καὶ ἀϊδίου ὑπάρξεως, εἰ καὶ τὸν Πατέρα ἀρχὴν εἶχεν ὡς αἰτίαν τῆς αὐτοῦ θείας ὑπάρξεως.

Χαίροις, Σιών, τὸ θεῖον ὄρος τὸ ἅγιον, ἐν ᾧ κατῴκει τὸ θεῖον ὄρος τὸ ἔμψυχον· ἡ νέα Βαιθήλ, ἐν ᾗ στήλη ἤλειπται, ἀνθρωπίνη φύσις χριομένη θεότητι. Ἐκ σοῦ πρὸς οὐράνιον ὕψος μετεώρισται, ὡς ἐξ ἐλαιῶν, ὁ ταύτης Υἱός.

Ἑτοιμαζέσθω νεφέλη παγκόσμιός τε καὶ περικόσμιος, καὶ ἀνέμων πτέρυγες ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς πρὸς Σιὼν τοὺς ἀποστόλους διαβιβάζουσαι. Τίνες οἵδε ὡσεὶ νεφέλαι καὶ ἀετοὶ πέτανται πρὸς τὸ πτῶμα τὸ τῆς πάντων ἀναστάσεως αἴτιον τῇ Μητρὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ λειτουργήσοντες; Τίς αὕτη ἡ ἀναβαίνουσα λελευκανθισμένη, ὅλη καλή, ἐκλάμπουσα ὡς ἥλιος; Ἀδέτωσαν αἱ κιθάραι τοῦ Πνεύματος, ἀποστολικαὶ γλῶσσαι. Ἀλαλαζέτωσαν κύμβαλα, αἱ τῶν θεολόγων ἀκρότητες, τὸ σκεῦος τῆς ἐκλογῆς Ἱερόθεος, ὁ τῷ θείῳ καθιερωμένος Πνεύματι, ὁ τῇ θείᾳ ἑνώσει τὰ θεῖα παθὼν καὶ μαθών, ὅλος ἐξιστάσθω τοῦ σώματος· ὅλος συνεκδημείτω τῇ προαιρέσει, καὶ κροτείτω τοῖς ἐφυμνίοις.

Πάντα τὰ ἔθνη χεῖρας κροτείτωσαν, πάντες τὴν Θεοτόκον ὑμνείτωσαν. Ἄγγελοι θνητῷ λειτουργείτωσαν σώματι. Θυγατέρες Ἱερουσαλήμ, ὀπίσω τῆς βασιλίδος ἀκολουθήσατε, καὶ ὡς πλησίον αὐτῆς παρθένοι νεανιευόμεναι Πνεύματι πρὸς τὸν νυμφίον συναπενέχθητε, ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ Δεσπότου παραστησόμεναι.

Κάτιθι, κάτιθι, Δέσποτα, τῇ Μητρὶ κατάχρεως ἀποτιννὺς τὰ ὀφειλόμενα θρέπτρα. Θείας ἀνάπετασον χεῖρας· δέξαι ψυχὴν μητρικήν, ὁ πατρικαῖς χερσὶ τὸ πνεῦμα ἐπὶ σταυροῦ παραθέμενος, φώνησον πρὸς αὐτὴν ἡδύ τι ψιθύρισμα. Ἐλθέ, ἡ καλή, ἡ πλησίον μου, ἡ τῷ κάλλει τῆς παρθενίας ὑπὲρ ἥλιον μαρμαρύσσουσα. Μετέδωκάς μοι τῶν σῶν· δεῦρο, τῶν ἐμῶν συναπόλαυσον· δεῦρο, Μῆτερ, πρὸς τὸν Υἱόν· δεῦρο, συμβασίλευσον τῷ ἐκ σοῦ σὺν σοὶ πτωχεύσαντι. Ἄπιθι, Δέσποινα, ἄπιθι, οὐ Μωσαϊκῶς, ἀνάβα, καὶ τελεύτα. Τελεύτα δὲ μᾶλλον, καὶ οὕτως ἀνάβαινε. Ψυχὴν παράθου ταῖς τοῦ Υἱοῦ σου χερσίν. Ἀπόδος τὸ τοῦ χοὸς τῷ χοΐ, ὡς ὅτι τοῦτο συνεπαρθήσεται.

Ἄρατε, ὁ τοῦ Θεοῦ λαός, τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν, ἄρατε. Ἰδοὺ ἐν Σιὼν ἡ κιβωτὸς Κυρίου Θεοῦ τῶν δυνάμεων, καὶ ταύτῃ σωματικῶς οἱ ἀπόστολοι παρειστήκεισαν τὸ ζωαρχικὸν καὶ θεοδόχον σῶμα κηδεύοντες. Ἀΰλως δὲ καὶ ἀοράτως περιέπουσιν ἄγγελοι φόβῳ, τῇ Μητρὶ τοῦ σφῶν Δεσπότου δουλοπρεπῶς παριστάμενοι. Αὐτὸς ὁ Κύριος πάρεστιν, ὁ πανταχοῦ παρών, καὶ τὰ πάντα πληρῶν, καὶ περιέπων τὸ πᾶν, οὗ τόπος οὐδείς. Ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ τὰ πάντα ὡς ποιητικῷ καὶ συνεκτικῷ αἰτίῳ.

Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος, ἡ θυγάτηρ Ἀδὰμ καὶ Μήτηρ Θεοῦ, δι' Ἀδὰμ τὸ σῶμα παραπέμπει τῇ γῇ, τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν οὐρανίαις σκηναῖς διὰ τὸν Υἱὸν ἀναδίδωσιν. Ἁγιαζέσθω τὸ ἄστυ τὸ ἅγιον, καὶ ἐπ' εὐλογίαις καρπούσθω εὐλογίαν αἰώνιον. Τῇ διαβάσει τοῦ θείου σκηνώματος προπορευέσθωσαν ἄγγελοι, καὶ τὸν τάφον εὐτρεπιζέτωσαν. Κοσμείτω τοῦτον αἴγλη τοῦ Πνεύματος. Ἑτοιμαζέσθω μύρα, καὶ τῷ παναμώμῳ καὶ πανευώδει μυριζέσθωσαν σώματι. Παρήτω νᾶμα εἰλικρινές, καὶ ἀρυέσθω τὴν εὐλογίαν ἐκ τῆς ἀκηράτου τῆς εὐλογίας πηγῆς. Ἀγαλλιάσθω ἡ γῆ τῇ καταθέσει τοῦ σώματος. Ἀὴρ σκιρτάτω τῇ ἀναβάσει τοῦ Πνεύματος. Πνείτωσαν αὖραι δροσοειδεῖς, καὶ χάριτος ἔμπλεοι. Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις πανηγυριζέτω τὴν τῆς Θεομήτορος ἄνοδον. Χοροὶ νέων ἀλαλαζέτωσαν. Ῥυήτωσαν γλῶσσαι ῥητόρων τοῖς ἐφυμνίοις· καρδίαι σοφῶν τὸ θαῦμα φιλοσοφείτωσαν· πρεσβῦται τῇ πολιᾷ τὸ αἰδέσιμον ἔχοντες, ἄτρεμα τὰς θεωρίας καρποφορείτωσαν. Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις συνεισενεγκάτω τὸν ἔρανον. Οὐδ' οὕτω γὰρ ἂν πολλοστοῦ μέρους τῆς ἀξίας ἐφίκοιντο.
pass_a_gloss: [0] Today she takes (λαμβάνει) a beginning (ἀρχή) of a second existence (ὕπαρξις) from the one having given her the beginning of the first existence, she having given (δοῦσα) a beginning of a second (existence), the bodily (σωματική) existence I mean, to the one not having had a temporal (χρονική) beginning of the first and eternal (ἀΐδιος) existence, even if he had the Father as beginning, as cause (αἰτία) of his divine existence. [1] Hail/rejoice (χαίροις), Zion (Σιών), the divine holy mountain (ὄρος), in which dwelt (κατῴκει) the divine living mountain; the new Bethel (Βαιθήλ), in which a pillar (στήλη) has been anointed (ἤλειπται), human nature (φύσις) being anointed (χριομένη) with Godhead (θεότης). From you to heavenly height (ὕψος) has been raised, as from the olives, the Son of this one (ταύτης). [2] Let be prepared a cloud (νεφέλη) all-world and around-world, and wings (πτέρυγες) of winds (ἄνεμοι) from the ends (πέρατα) of the earth to Zion carrying across the apostles. Who are these, as clouds and eagles (ἀετοί), (who) fly (πέτανται) to the corpse/body (πτῶμα), the cause of the resurrection of all, to serve the Mother of God? Who is this, the one going up, made white, all beautiful (ὅλη καλή), shining out as the sun? Let sing the harps (κιθάραι) of the Spirit, apostolic tongues. Let cymbals (κύμβαλα) shout aloud, the summits of the theologians (θεολόγοι), the vessel (σκεῦος) of election (ἐκλογή) Hierotheus (Ἱερόθεος), the one consecrated to the divine Spirit, the one having by the divine union (ἕνωσις) suffered and learned the divine things, let him wholly stand out of the body; wholly let him go abroad with by choice, and let him clap/strike (κροτείτω) to the refrains (ἐφύμνια). [3] All the nations (ἔθνη) let them clap hands, all let them hymn the Theotokos. Angels let them minister to a mortal (θνητόν) body. Daughters of Jerusalem, follow behind (ὀπίσω) the queen (βασιλίς), and as virgins near (πλησίον) her, being youthful in Spirit, to the bridegroom (νυμφίος) be carried along together, to stand at the right (δεξιά) of the Master (Δεσπότης). [4] Come down (κάτιθι), come down, Master, to the Mother as a debtor paying back the owed nursing-wages (θρέπτρα). Spread out divine hands; receive (δέξαι) a motherly (μητρική) soul (ψυχή), you who into paternal (πατρικαί) hands committed the spirit (πνεῦμα) on the cross (σταυρός); call (φώνησον) to her some sweet whisper: Come (ἐλθέ), the beautiful one, the one near me, the one by the beauty (κάλλος) of virginity (παρθενία) above the sun flashing. You gave me a share (μετέδωκας) of yours; come (δεῦρο), enjoy with mine; come, Mother, to the Son; come, co-reign with the one from you with you having become poor. Depart (ἄπιθι), Lady (Δέσποινα), depart, not in Moses' manner (Μωσαϊκῶς), 'go up, and die'. Rather die, and so go up (ἀνάβαινε). The soul commit (παράθου) to the hands of your Son. Give back (ἀπόδος) the (thing) of dust (χοῦς) to dust, since (ὡς ὅτι) this will be taken up together. [5] Lift up (ἄρατε), people of God, your eyes, lift up. Behold (ἰδού) in Zion the ark (κιβωτός) of the Lord God of the powers, and by it bodily (σωματικῶς) the apostles stood, burying the life-originating (ζωαρχικόν) and God-receiving (θεοδόχον) body. Immaterially (ἀΰλως) and invisibly (ἀοράτως) angels tend (it) with fear (φόβος), standing by the Mother of their own Master as slaves befit. The Lord himself is present (πάρεστιν), the one present everywhere (πανταχοῦ), and filling (πληρῶν) all things, and encompassing (περιέπων) the all, whose place (τόπος) (is) none. For in him all things, as in the making (ποιητικόν) and holding-together cause (αἴτιον). [6] Behold the Virgin, the daughter of Adam and Mother of God, through (because of) Adam the body sends on to the earth, but the soul to heavenly tents/dwellings (σκηναί) through (because of) the Son gives up. Let be sanctified (ἁγιαζέσθω) the holy city (ἄστυ), and upon blessings (εὐλογίαι) let it reap (καρπούσθω) an eternal blessing. At the passage (διάβασις) of the divine tabernacle (σκήνωμα) let angels go before, and let them make ready the tomb. Let adorn (κοσμείτω) it the radiance (αἴγλη) of the Spirit. Let ointments (μύρα) be prepared, and on the all-blameless (πανάμωμος) and all-fragrant (πανευώδης) body let them be poured as perfume. Let be present a pure stream (νᾶμα), and let it draw (ἀρυέσθω) the blessing from the undefiled (ἀκήρατος) spring (πηγή) of the blessing. Let exult the earth at the deposition (κατάθεσις) of the body. Let the air leap (σκιρτάτω) at the ascent (ἀνάβασις) of the spirit. Let breezes (αὖραι) blow (πνείτωσαν) dewy and full of grace (χάρις). Let all creation (κτίσις) keep festival for the going-up (ἄνοδος) of the Mother of God (Θεομήτωρ). Let choirs of young ones (νέοι) shout aloud. Let flow (ῥυήτωσαν) tongues of orators (ῥήτορες) with refrains (ἐφύμνια); let hearts of the wise philosophize the wonder (θαῦμα); let elders, having with grey hair (πολιά) the venerable (αἰδέσιμον), steadily/quietly (ἄτρεμα) bear fruit as to contemplations (θεωρίαι). Let all creation bring together the contribution (ἔρανος). For not even so would they reach (ἐφίκοιντο) the least part of the worth (ἀξία).

lemmas.greek: ἐκ σοῦ; Germ. and Allatius ἐξ οὗ, 'from which'
ἐλαιῶν, i.e. the Mount of Olives

pass_b_english: Today she receives the beginning of a second existence from him who gave her the beginning of her first existence: she who gave the beginning of a second existence, I mean bodily existence, to him who had no beginning in time of his first and eternal existence, even though he had the Father as his beginning, as the cause of his divine existence.

Rejoice, Zion, holy mountain of God, in which the living mountain of God dwelt; the new Bethel, in which a pillar has been anointed (Genesis 28:18–19), human nature anointed with the Godhead. From you her Son was raised up to the height of heaven, as from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:9–12).

Let a cloud be made ready, as wide as the world and encircling it, and wings of winds to carry the apostles across from the ends of the earth to Zion. Who are these that fly like clouds (Isaiah 60:8) and like eagles to the body (Matthew 24:28) that is the cause of resurrection for all, to serve the Mother of God? Who is this who comes up, all in white (Song of Songs 8:5), all fair (Song of Songs 4:7), shining like the sun (Song of Songs 6:10)? Let the harps of the Spirit sing, the tongues of the apostles. Let the cymbals sound aloud, the foremost of the theologians. Let Hierotheus, the chosen vessel (Acts 9:15), consecrated to the divine Spirit, who in divine union both underwent and learned divine things, go wholly out of the body; let him wholly go forth with her in his will, and beat time to the refrains.

Let all the nations clap their hands (Psalm 47:1); let all sing hymns to the Mother of God. Let angels serve a mortal body. Daughters of Jerusalem, follow after the queen, and as virgins near her, youthful in the Spirit, be brought along with her to the Bridegroom (Psalm 45:14), to stand at the right hand of the Master (Psalm 45:9).

Come down, come down, Master, and as one in her debt repay your Mother what is owed for your nursing. Spread out your divine hands; receive your mother's soul, you who on the cross committed your spirit into your Father's hands (Luke 23:46). Speak to her some sweet whisper: “Come, my fair one, my close one (Song of Songs 2:10), you who shine brighter than the sun with the beauty of virginity. You gave me a share in what is yours; come, enjoy with me what is mine. Come, Mother, to your Son; come, reign with him who, born of you, became poor with you (2 Corinthians 8:9).” Depart, Lady, depart; not as Moses did, “Go up, and die” (Deuteronomy 32:49–50), but rather die, and so go up. Commit your soul into the hands of your Son. Give back to the dust what belongs to the dust, since it will be taken up along with you.

Lift up your eyes, people of God, lift them up. See, the ark of the Lord God of hosts is in Zion, and the apostles stood beside it in the body, burying the body that is the source of life and that received God. Immaterially and invisibly, angels attend it in awe, standing by the Mother of their own Master as servants. The Lord himself is present, he who is present everywhere, fills all things and encompasses the universe, who is in no place; for all things are in him (Colossians 1:17), as in the cause that makes them and holds them together.

See, the Virgin, the daughter of Adam and Mother of God, because of Adam gives her body over to the earth, but because of her Son gives up her soul to the dwellings of heaven. Let the holy city be sanctified, and in addition to its blessings let it reap an eternal blessing. As the divine tabernacle passes, let angels go before it and make the tomb ready. Let the radiance of the Spirit adorn it. Let perfumes be prepared and poured over the all-blameless and all-fragrant body. Let a pure stream be at hand and draw blessing from the undefiled spring of blessing. Let the earth rejoice at the laying down of the body. Let the air leap at the going up of the spirit. Let breezes blow, dewy and full of grace. Let all creation keep festival for the going up of the Mother of God. Let choirs of the young shout for joy. Let the tongues of orators flow with hymns; let the hearts of the wise reflect on the wonder; let the old, whose grey hair is worthy of respect, quietly bring forth the fruit of their contemplation. Let all creation bring its share to the common feast. For not even so would they reach the smallest part of what she deserves.

choices.note: Psalm renumbering: Psalm 47:1 = LXX/Vulgate Psalm 46:2 ('All the nations, clap your hands').
Psalm 45:14 = LXX/Vulgate Psalm 44:15 (Migne's margin 'Psal.
XLIV, 15': virgins brought after the queen, her companions);
Psalm 45:9 = LXX 44:10 (the queen stands at the right hand).
Song of Songs 8:5 LXX is quoted word for word ('Who is this who comes up, made white'); 4:7 'all fair'; 6:10 'chosen as the sun', here 'shining like the sun'.
Isaiah 60:8 LXX ('Who are these that fly like clouds') joined with Matthew 24:28 (eagles gathering to the body, πτῶμα), both clear.
Acts 9:15 'chosen vessel' is Paul's title, applied here to Hierotheus (the Latin reads it so: 'Vas electionis Hierotheus');
Migne's margin points to Dionysius, Divine Names 3, for Hierotheus 'suffering, not only learning, divine things' (not Scripture, not cited inline).
Genesis 28:18-19 for the anointed pillar at Bethel;
Acts 1:9-12 for the ascension from the Mount of Olives.
Deuteronomy 32:49-50 LXX ('go up ... and die on the mountain').
Luke 23:46 for the spirit committed into the Father's hands;
Song of Songs 2:10 LXX ('Come, my close one, my fair one'); 2 Corinthians 8:9 (he became poor) cited as a clear echo of πτωχεύσαντι;
Colossians 1:17 for all things held together in him (συνεκτικῷ).

Left uncited as possible only: Psalm 150:5 (cymbals), Psalm 104:3 / 18:10 (wings of the wind), Isaiah 60:4 (lift up your eyes), Genesis 3:19 / Ecclesiastes 12:7 (dust to dust), Jeremiah 23:24 / Ephesians 4:10 (fills all things), 2 Samuel 6 (the ark in Zion).
Readings: ἀρχή rendered 'beginning' throughout section [0] to keep John's play on the word, including 'he had the Father as his beginning, as the cause'.
ὁ ταύτης Υἱός rendered 'her Son' (Mary, the living mountain; grammatically ταύτης could refer to the nearer 'human nature', which makes poor sense).
Migne note (70): ἐξ οὗ ('from which') in the Germanus codex and Allatius for ἐκ σοῦ;
English follows the print.
Printed Ἀδέτωσαν read as ᾀδέτωσαν;
κατάχρεως rendered 'as one in her debt';
θρέπτρα ('return for nurture') rendered 'what is owed for your nursing'.
Παρήτω read as from πάρειμι ('be at hand').
τῇ ἀναβάσει τοῦ Πνεύματος: Migne capitalizes Πνεύματος, but in contrast with the body laid in earth it is most naturally her spirit going up; rendered lowercase 'the spirit'.
If the Holy Spirit is meant, read 'the Spirit'.
ἔρανος (a shared contribution to a common meal) rendered 'its share to the common feast'.
Migne note (71) at ἄρατε: Allatius's Latin translation adds a long passage taken from Andrew of Crete's second homily, absent from both Greek codices;
Migne prints no extra Greek and nothing is supplied here.
Reviewer: αἱ τῶν θεολόγων ἀκρότητες ('the foremost of the theologians', plural) stands with the cymbals;
Hierotheus (nominative) is the subject of ἐξιστάσθω, so he starts a new sentence rather than being equated with 'the summits'.
παθὼν καὶ μαθών rendered 'both underwent and learned', in the Greek order, without importing Dionysius's 'not only ... but' frame.
τῇ προαιρέσει with συνεκδημείτω rendered 'in his will' (in intent, since he goes with her in spirit).
περιέπων τὸ πᾶν 'encompasses the universe';
οὗ τόπος οὐδείς 'who is in no place'.

Ἀδέτωσαν αἱ κιθάραι τοῦ') and all of col. 760 (PDF leaf 421, right column, from 'Πνεύματος, ἀποστολικαὶ γλῶσσαι' to 'ἐφίκοιντο.').
